newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share prices end sharply higher on rates, NZD.
newsitem.headline: NZ share prices end sharply higher on rates, NZD.

text.p: New Zealand share prices ended strongly on Wednesday on high turnover as investors continued to take heart from a lower interest and exchange rate environment.
Yield-sensitive Telecom led the way, gaining 17 cents to NZ$6.73, followed closely by Fletcher Paper, up seven at $3.36.
Most other leaders were also stronger, pushing the NZSE-40 Capital Index up 23.13 points (1.0 percent) to 2,328.37 on turnover worth NZ$79.5 million.

"Although (monetary) settings are pretty much where they were yesterday at the long end, I think overall that offshore investors are taking some comfort that the positive influence on interest rates will flow ultimately into the market," said Murray Rutherford of SBC Warburg.
"There has been a structural move in interest rates which does always spill over into the equity market," he said.
Rutherford noted that Telecom's annual result was due next week and said all the bad news appeared to be out after the utility reported its third quarter result.
Outside the leading issues, Sanford was sold down by 50 cents (17.86 percent) to NZ$2.30 after a surprisingly dismal first half result on Tuesday.
But there was significant private client support for some of the other smaller issues.
Among these were Waste Management, up 25 to NZ$6.25 and Baycorp Holdings up 20 at $4.20. Waste Management holds its annual meeting on Thursday.
